definition: In this context, an emergency intervention is an urgent response used during an acute suicidal crisis. It is treated as a serious suicidal event, distinct from a suicide attempt but indicating immediate crisis-level risk.

reasons: The packet supports that an emergency intervention occurs for an acute suicidal crisis and is counted among “suicidal events,” but it does not support defining it as a general “urgent response” or as a clinical intervention procedure.

The packet does support that it is distinct from a suicide attempt, but it does not say it is a diagnosis- or risk-level category on its own, so the phrasing “treated as a serious suicidal event” needs tighter grounding in the source.

The packet defines “suicidal events” as “either a suicide attempt or an emergency intervention for an acute suicidal crisis,” but it does not state that an emergency intervention is an “urgent response.”
The packet does not explicitly characterize an “emergency intervention” as “treated as a serious suicidal event.” (It is only included as one type of “suicidal events.”)

While the packet indicates emergency intervention is distinct from a suicide attempt by listing them as separate alternatives within “suicidal events,” it does not support the added claim that it “indicat[es] immediate crisis-level risk” beyond the phrase “for an acute suicidal crisis.”
